title: Cyber Security Analyst
description: Cyber Security Analyst Not Disclosed Kingston and St. Andrew Not disclosed Permanent full-time Updated 18/11/2026 HR Manager Apply Now Share Share this job Facebook Twitter Report This Job Save Save Join our team as a Cybersecurity Analyst and help protect our systems, data and digital assets from evolving threats. ROLE & CORE FUNCTONS The Cybersecurity Analyst is responsible for supporting the organisation’s cybersecurity programme by helping to protect information systems, digital assets, and technology platforms from security risks and threats. This is a hands‑on technical role that contributes to the design, implementation, and operation of security controls across infrastructure, applications, cloud services, and user access. The role works closely with IT and business stakeholders to ensure security controls are effective, proportionate, and aligned with recognised international standards and best practices. FUNCTIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES Support the day-to-day operation and continuous improvement of cybersecurity controls protecting the organization’s systems, networks, applications, and data. Analyze security events, identity risks, access anomalies, vulnerabilities, and emerging threats from internal and external sources; provide risk-based recommendations and executive-ready reporting. Assist with the implementation, configuration, optimization, and integration of security tools and platforms, including IAM, PAM (e.g., CyberArk), SIEM, IGA, and Zero Trust policy engines. Design, validate, and maintain Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) models aligned to business functions and regulatory requirements. Analyze and review user and system access to ensure entitlements are appropriate, aligned to approved role profiles, and compliant with segregation-of-duties principles. Identify and remediate misaligned privileges, excessive access, dormant accounts, and privilege creep through continuous analytics and trend monitoring. Support implementation and monitoring of Privileged Access Management (PAM) and Just-in-Time (JIT) access workflows for high-risk roles. Develop and maintain security analytics dashboards and automated reporting for access certifications, high-risk privilege assignments, Zero Trust posture metrics, and audit requirements. Support the implementation and operationalization of Zero Trust Architecture across identity, device, network, and application layers, including behavioral baseline development and anomaly detection. Assist with data discovery, posture assessments, control effectiveness reviews, vulnerability assessments, and penetration testing exercises. Support secure system design and change initiatives, ensuring security requirements and Zero Trust principles are embedded in system development, infrastructure changes, and cloud adoption. Maintain and monitor security configuration baselines for operating systems, applications, and platforms. Provide audit-ready documentation and evidence to support internal audits, regulatory examinations, and cybersecurity governance reporting. Participate as a subject matter contributor in security initiatives, incident reviews, investigations involving identity or access misuse, and continuous improvement activities. Work collaboratively with infrastructure, application, HR, compliance, and operations teams to promote secure-by-design practices and effective access governance. Support compliance with cybersecurity policies, standards, regulatory requirements, and enterprise risk management frameworks. QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE Bachelor’s Degree in Cyber-Security/Computer Science/Information Technology or related field. Minimum of 5 years IT experience including 2 year of information security focus. Knowledge of IT infrastructure including networking, communication, firewalls, VPNs and key IT systems and configuration. Superior understanding of current and evolving technologies and technology security related trends Operational knowledge and hands on experience implementing best practices standards such as ISO 27000, COBIT, NIST, PCI DSS, GDPR and other security control frameworks.
